question:
Do the native VCell hybrid solver and the process-bigraph co-simulation both reproduce
Fig 1B of Schaff et al. (2016)? The error of the trial-mean calcium against its exact
expectation should fall as N^-1/2 with the number of trials, and be statistically
dominated at small Δt.
hypothesis:
The channels' gating is independent of calcium, so E[U] solves the linear PDE driven by
the exact open probability p(t) = k_on/(k_on+k_off)·(1 − e^-(k_on+k_off)t). Both solvers'
trial means converge to it with ε ∝ N^-1/2. At N = 128 the statistical error dominates
the Δt error for Δt ≤ 0.02 s. The two solvers differ only by sampling.
objective:
Model (Eq. 1 of the paper): ∂U/∂t = D∇²U + J·Σᵢ ξᵢ δ(r − rᵢ) − V_p(U − U₀), no-flux
boundaries. D = 1 µm²/s, J = 10 µM·µm³/s, U₀ = 0.1 µM, V_p = 1 s⁻¹, k_on = 1 s⁻¹,
k_off = 5 s⁻¹, 24 channels starting closed, T = 5 s.
Geometry: [0, 10.1]×[0, 2.1]×[0, 0.5] µm³, Δx = Δy = 0.1.
Runs: 128 trials per solver at Δt ∈ {0.02, 0.01, 0.005} s. ε(N) is taken from nested
subsets at Δt = 0.005, and ε is the RMS over space and time of (trial mean − E[U]),
relative to max(E[U] − U₀).
description:
Channels are immobile particle species C (closed) and O (open), one per channel node.
Calcium U is a PDE field, and influx is a PDE source k·[O] with k = J·602.214.
- The native reference goes through VCell's own math generation (pyvcell → libvcell
  → vcell-fvsolver/Smoldyn 2.38), with two documented .smoldynInput post-processing
  steps (viva_pde_particle.reference.vcell_native):
  1. channels are placed at their nodes, because a BioModel cannot express per-node
     particle counts;
  2. VCell's no-op jump process O → O (from the influx) is dropped. In Smoldyn it would
     suppress channel closing (competing first-order reactions), which raises the open
     fraction from 1/6 to about 0.9.
- The reference E[U] is computed on the same grid with a fine step (dt_ref = 1e-4).

Deviations from the paper, both PROVISIONAL:
- Δz = 0.25 (3 z-nodes). Current VCell requires at least 3 nodes per axis; the paper
  used Δz = 0.5.
- Channel coordinates: the paper shows 4 columns of 6 (Fig 1A) without coordinates.
  Here, x = 2, 4, 6, 8 µm and y = 0.3 ... 1.8 µm on the z = 0 layer (approved by the
  author for now).

conclusion:
Reproduced on both solvers (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-03; run in the dev pixi env):
- ε vs N slopes: −0.46 for both solvers, against −1/2;
- ε at N = 128: 1.37% (co-sim) and 1.32% (native);
- ε is flat across Δt = 0.02–0.005 s (1.3–1.6%), i.e. statistically dominated, as in the paper;
- co-sim vs native difference: 0.75× the combined statistical error.

Two VCell findings for the native path, both handled in vcell_native.to_biomodel and
in post-processing:
- **No-op jump process** (virtualcell/vcell#2158): a particle catalysing a continuous
  source produces a no-op Smoldyn reaction that suppresses channel closing.
- **Zero-reactant mass action:** VCell keeps only −Kr·Π(products) and discards Kf, so
  the constant leak V_p·U₀ vanished. It is now written as General kinetics. An earlier
  run without this fix gave a native ε(128) of 1.6%.

findings.statement: Both solvers reproduce Fig 1B's Monte-Carlo convergence: the log-log slope of ε vs N is −0.47 (co-simulation) and −0.46 (native VCell hybrid), both within sampling of the theoretical −1/2.
findings.next_action: None — convergence rate confirmed on both solvers.

findings.statement: At N=128, Δt=0.005 s the error is small and essentially solver-independent: ε=1.37% (co-sim) vs 1.32% (native), and ε is flat across Δt=0.02–0.005 s (1.3–1.6%) — i.e. statistically dominated, exactly as the paper reports.

The co-simulation and native solvers agree to within sampling: their trial-mean difference is 0.75× the combined statistical error (<1.5), so decomposing the hybrid solver into process-bigraph processes does not change the answer. Reaching this required two documented VCell fixes in the native path (no-op jump process virtualcell/vcell#2158; zero-reactant mass-action leak).
findings.next_action: Carry the two VCell fixes upstream; revisit the provisional Δz=0.25 and channel coordinates once VCell supports Δz=0.5 and per-node particle counts.

regression_compatibility.basis: results/metrics.json is committed and regenerated by sims/run.py; all four behavior tests pass against it.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces Schaff et al. 2016 Fig 1B on both solvers: N^-1/2 convergence, ε≈1.3% at N=128, statistically-dominated Δt dependence.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-03 shows the process-bigraph decomposition is answer-preserving (0.75× combined error) and localizes the two VCell encoding fixes needed to make the native reference match.

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: Both solvers reproduce Fig 1B (N^-1/2 convergence, ε≈1.3% at N=128, Δt-dominated by sampling) and agree to within sampling — the process-bigraph decomposition is answer-preserving. Carry the two VCell encoding fixes upstream and lift the provisional Δz / channel-coordinate deviations when VCell supports them.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: A slope outside [−0.75, −0.25], ε(128) ≥ 3%, or a cosim-vs-native ratio ≥ 1.5 would mean the decomposition or the native encoding changed the answer — re-examine the VCell math generation (no-op jump, zero-reactant mass action) before trusting the arm.

report.caveat: Two deviations from the paper remain provisional (Δz=0.25 vs 0.5; channel coordinates chosen, author-approved). The native arm needs the dev pixi env.
